faq.a: Abdelkader is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ الْقَادِر, whose core sense is abdelkader; servant of the capable.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdelkader?
faq.a: Abdelkader is associated with Arabic. Abdelkader is Arabic عَبْدُ الْقَادِر (ʿAbd al-Qādir), meaning 'servant of the Capable'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ الْقَادِر is Arabic.
Abdelkader can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdelkader should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd al-Qādir is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdelkader mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdelkader is rendered عبدالقادر and carries the sense عبدالقادر، قادر کا بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdelkader mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdelkader is rendered عبدالقادر and carries the sense عبدالقادر، بنده قادر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-del-ka-der. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.
